prompt: Split a raw command line into options and positional arguments, honouring the convention that a lone -- ends option parsing and everything after it is positional.
explanation: Real command lines mix three kinds of token, so each argument is classified in a fixed order: the lone "--" separator first, then anything starting with "--" as an option, then everything else as positional. A boolean flag remembers that the separator has been seen, which is what makes a later "--not-an-option" positional rather than an option. Splitting on the first '=' via indexOf and two substrings separates the name from the value, and a LinkedHashMap keeps insertion order while letting a repeated key overwrite the earlier value.
hints: Test arg.equals("--") BEFORE arg.startsWith("--"), otherwise the separator looks like an option with an empty name.
Strip the leading dashes with arg.substring(2), then use indexOf('=') on what is left: -1 means a bare flag worth "true".
Track a boolean afterSeparator; once it is true, options() ignores everything and positionals() takes everything.
